summary: Response-cache writes go to a same-directory temporary file and are renamed into place, so a concurrent reader never observes a partial body.
reason: Cache refresh removed the old file and wrote the replacement directly to the final path, so a second CLI process refreshing or reading the same uncached resource could read a truncated body and treat malformed JSON as a successful cache hit. Rename is atomic within a filesystem; os.CreateTemp already creates 0600, matching the previous permissions.
validated_outcome: go test ./internal/client/ -run TestWriteCacheIsAtomic hammers concurrent reads and writes and asserts every successful read is complete valid JSON with no .tmp- leftovers.
